renderings.value: Expresses 'whether A or B'; both situations are included.

The grammar point ～AかれBかれ is a somewhat literary/old-fashioned pattern often seen with i-adjectives (e.g., 早かれ遅かれ). It can mean 'whether A or B'. Here it's shown with nouns or verbs, which is also possible in older or set expressions.
Commonly i-adjective stems + かれ + i-adjective stems + かれ (e.g. 早かれ遅かれ). Also sometimes Noun + かれ + Noun + かれ in older usage.
Formal, literary - one of several near-interchangeable "whether A or B" constructions; stylistic choice more than a formality ladder.
Whether it's winter or summer, I jog every day.
Whether he comes or not, the party will start.
Whether we win or lose, it's important to take part in the match.
Whether it's raining or snowing, I never skip walking the dog.
